transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

My doctor thought I should come in. She’s concerned my meal planning has gotten… too strict, I guess. I don’t really see it that way. I usually just have yogurt for breakfast, skip lunch if I’m busy, and keep dinner measured so the day feels orderly.
Do you feel anxious or upset if you're unable to follow your usual eating plan?

A little, yes. If I have a normal dinner out or something and the scale is up even a pound after, I get… pretty panicky. Like I’ve let things get out of control, and I need to make it right the next day.
Do you think about your weight or body shape when deciding what or how much to eat?

Yes… I suppose I do. Not in a trying-to-look-young way. It’s more that I notice whether my waist and hips look… contained, I guess, in my clothes. If they don’t, I take that as a sign I’m not handling things well.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?
Yes… I suppose I am. If the scale is up even a pound after a normal dinner, especially eating out, I get this sudden panic. Like I’ve lost control and have to fix it the next day.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently?

Some, yes. My doctor seems to think it’s more than it should be. I don’t always see it that way, though… when I look at the number, I still think maybe a little lower would feel neater. More manageable.
Do you feel like you would lose control if you weren't restricting your food intake?

I… maybe. I don’t think of it as losing control exactly. It’s more that if I don’t keep things planned—yogurt for breakfast, maybe no lunch if I’m busy, and a measured dinner—the day feels too loose. The planning keeps it orderly.
Is your main goal in restricting your food intake to avoid gaining weight or to feel more in control of your daily life?

I think… more the control part, maybe. I came in because my doctor thought my meal planning had gotten too tight. To me it just feels like keeping things orderly—yogurt for breakfast, maybe skipping lunch if I’m busy, and a very measured dinner.
When you think about your eating plan, is it more about achieving a specific weight or body shape, or is it about maintaining a sense of control and order in your daily life?

I suppose it’s more the order of it. My doctor thinks the planning has gotten too tight, but to me it’s just… yogurt in the morning, lunch if it fits—or not if I’m busy—and a measured dinner. It makes the day feel contained.
Do you think your fear of gaining weight is what drives you to plan your meals so strictly?

Maybe… yes, somewhat. I don’t like admitting that.

If the scale is up even a pound after a normal dinner, or eating out, I get this sudden panic. Like I’ve lost control and have to make up for it the next day.
Are you trying to reach a specific weight with your eating plan?

Not a specific weight exactly… but my weight has gone down more than my doctor likes. And when I look at the chart, I do catch myself thinking maybe just a little lower would be… cleaner, easier to manage.
Do you think being thinner would make you happier or more successful?

Happier or successful… I don’t know if I’d say it that plainly.

I’m not trying to look young or anything. But I do notice I judge how well I’m managing myself by whether my waist and hips feel… contained in my clothes. It’s hard to explain.
Do you feel that your self-worth is closely tied to your weight or body shape?

Yes… more than I’d like to admit.

I know I’m older, and I’m not trying to look young. But I still sort of measure how I’m doing by whether my waist and hips look… contained in my clothes. If they don’t, I feel like I’m not handling myself well.
Is your restrictive eating more about preventing weight gain or about feeling in control of your life?

Probably both… but if I’m honest, it’s more that if the scale is up even a pound after a normal dinner or eating out, I panic. It feels like I’ve lost control, and then I feel like I have to make up for it the next day.
Which is stronger for you, the fear of gaining weight or the need to feel in control through your eating plan?

The fear of gaining weight, I think.

The control part is there, but… if the scale is even up a pound after a normal dinner or eating out, I get this sharp panic. Like I’ve done something wrong and need to fix it the next day.
Is your restrictive eating pattern something you feel you could stop if you weren't afraid of gaining weight?

I don’t think I could, no.

It’s really the weight part that sets it off. If the scale is up even a little after a normal dinner or going out to eat, I get this sharp panic… like I’ve lost control and have to correct it the next day.
Is the panic you feel when you gain weight more about the weight itself or the feeling that you've lost control of your eating plan?
More the weight itself, I think. The control feeling comes with it, but if the scale is up even a little after dinner out or something, I panic and feel like I have to fix it the next day.
Is the weight gain you fear more about the actual number on the scale or how your body would look and feel at that weight?
It’s more the number, I think. If it’s even up a pound after a normal dinner or eating at a restaurant, I get this panic… like I’ve lost control and need to make up for it the next day.
When you restrict your food intake, is it primarily because you are afraid of what will happen if you gain weight?
Yes… mostly. If I see the scale go up even a pound after a normal dinner or eating out, I get really panicky, like I’ve lost control. Then I feel like I need to make up for it the next day.
Is your restrictive eating pattern something you would continue even if you weren't afraid of gaining weight?

I’m not sure. I tell myself it’s more about keeping things orderly… yogurt for breakfast, maybe no lunch if I’m busy, and then a measured dinner. But I suppose if weight weren’t part of it, maybe I wouldn’t be quite so strict.
Is the primary reason you restrict your food intake to prevent weight gain or to maintain a sense of control over your life?
I think it’s mostly to prevent the weight gain… though it feels like control too. If the scale is up even a pound after dinner out, I panic and feel like I have to fix it the next day.
